MPC ticked up 0.66% to close at $393.52, continuing a modest recovery after steep losses earlier in the week. The stock fell sharply from September 18 to September 22 (down roughly 8.4%), then stabilized and began recovering over the last three trading days. The driver appears to be oil price volatility tied to geopolitical tension: crude fell nearly 8% last week on Iran-U.S. ceasefire talks, but today's move comes as Trump rejected Iran's conditional ceasefire offer, raising the prospect of renewed conflict and tighter oil supplies. With U.S. crude at $96.41 and world oil at $114.89, refiners benefit from processing spreads, though the 94% utilization rate shows the industry isn't strained yet.

The underlying story is a shift from de-escalation risk back to supply-shock risk. Saudi Arabia's crude exports have hit their highest level since the Iran conflict began despite attacks on its infrastructure, but any widening of the Middle East conflict threatens those supply lines and could push oil sharply higher — exactly the kind of supply shock that supports refiner margins and energy prices more broadly.
